transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-09
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (HelioCloud Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (HelioCloud Sr. Cloud Engineer), Sofia Martinez (HelioCloud Partnerships), Rajiv Menon (HelioCloud Security)
Link to collateral referenced: short notes - marketplace-manifest (https://redwood.internal/docs/marketplace-manifest), ref-arch diagram (link shared post-call)

Summary:
Redwood + HelioCloud technical sync to align on marketplace listing and joint reference architecture for a managed Redwood integration on HelioCloud's marketplace. Focus on packaging (Helm + OCI image), networking/VPC patterns, SSO & billing integration, KMS/encryption, and automated QA for the marketplace listing test harness. Action items captured and follow-ups scheduled.

Topics Covered:
- Marketplace manifest requirements and Helm chart expectations
- Reference architecture for private deployment via Helio VPC (VPC peering vs PrivateLink)
- Identity & access: SAML/SCIM, service principals, RBAC mapping
- Billing & metering hooks for marketplace usage reporting
- Security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
- CI test harness and acceptance criteria for listing

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the manifest and the ref arch. Um, Diego will drive the technical bits on packaging.
[00:22] Priya (HelioCloud): Thanks Maya, on our side Priya and Liam here, plus Rajiv for security questions. We wanted to make sure we cover the VPC patterns — we have multiple customers asking for both peering and private endpoints.
[00:35] Diego (Redwood): Cool. I'll start with the high-level - for marketplace we typically provide an OCI image plus a Helm chart. The manifest needs the usage metering hooks and the marketplace entitlements manifest. We have a sample in the docs, and we'll send a trimmed version after.
[01:05] Liam (HelioCloud): When you say usage metering hooks, is that a webhook to our billing API or do you support meter polling?
[01:18] Diego (Redwood): We support both; preferred pattern is webhook push for near real-time metric reporting to Helio's billing endpoint. There's a small sidecar we ship that can translate internal token usage to marketplace events — sometimes called the meter-proxy in our repo. Note: sometimes the auto-transcription in demos says 'meter proxy' as 'meta proxy' so just FYI.
[01:47] Priya: Ok, good. On networking, we have customers that require no egress, so private deployments are common. Can Redwood run inside our VPC as a managed app?
[02:05] Anika (Redwood): Yes, we have two main patterns: Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated capacity) via VPC peering or PrivateLink-style private endpoints; and private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed with our agent. For marketplace listing, we recommend documenting both patterns in the ref arch.
[02:30] Rajiv (HelioCloud): For private deployments we need end-to-end encryption and KMS integration. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:45] Diego: Yes, we can plug into external KMS/HSM — customers can provide keys and we use envelope encryption. We'll note the KMS integration steps in the playbook. Sometimes the demo notes say 'K-M-S' spelled out oddly in transcripts.
[03:10] Maya: Quick question on identity — Helio prefers SAML + SCIM for user provisioning. For marketplace we also need a service principal for the ingestion and meter hook. What do you need from us?
[03:25] Liam: We can provision a service principal and provide client ID/secret or certificate. We also support short-lived tokens via our IAM. Which is preferred?
[03:40] Diego: For the marketplace test harness, a service principal with cert-based auth is easiest to automate. For production we'll support both. We'll put example manifests for both flows.
[04:05] Priya: On running the integration tests, what's in Redwood's QA harness? We need to validate network policies and multi-tenant isolation before listing.
[04:20] Anika: Our CI harness runs a set of smoke and acceptance tests: deploy helm chart, run a sample workload, validate latency SLOs, validate KV cache persistence across restarts, and run a security scan. We can add Helio-specific network smoke tests (VPC peering, route tables, NACLs).
[04:48] Liam: Sounds good. Can you share the exact k8s versions and helm chart requirements? We run 1.27 at scale.
[05:00] Diego: We'll add compatibility matrix to the manifest. Current supported K8s versions: 1.24-1.28, cert-manager versions and CRDs listed. I'll include an explicit minimum.
[05:18] Rajiv: Regarding audit logs — we need CloudTrail style eventing to show who accessed the model/inference. Where does Redwood surface audit logs?
[05:30] Diego: We forward audit events to a configurable sink — S3, GCS, or your logging endpoint. For marketplace deployments we recommend a sidecar that sends events to the Helio logging endpoint. We'll include example FluentBit/FluentD config.
[05:52] Priya: Ok. On the listing page content, we want standardized copy and a joint benefits section. Who owns the marketing blurb?
[06:05] Maya: Redwood will draft the initial listing blurb and send to Sofia for sign-off. That's in the next steps.
[06:15] Sofia (HelioCloud): Great — we'll review and suggest edits. Also interested in co-marketing timing.
[06:25] Maya: We'll propose a launch plan after the integration tests pass.
[06:32] 
[06:40] Diego: Now diving deeper into the manifest items — there are required fields in Helio's marketplace schema: publisher_id, package_version, install_instructions, entitlements, and a notarization checksum. We map those to our CI so the pipeline produces the checksum artifact.
[07:05] Liam: For entitlements, Helio needs to know which API calls map to metering units. How do you classify tokens vs embeddings?
[07:20] Diego: We tag usage events with unit_type (tokens, embeddings, rerank calls) in the meter-proxy payload. We'll provide the mapping and sample payload.
[07:40] Rajiv: Security Q — what's the attack surface of the meter-proxy? Can it be run in its own namespace with strict RBAC?
[07:55] Anika: Yes, meter-proxy can be deployed in a dedicated namespace with limited perms. We'll include a NetworkPolicy example and PodSecurityPolicy equivalents.
[08:20] Priya: On deployment options, what about onboarding complexity for customers who want Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private? We need clear decision tree for our sales engineering folks.
[08:35] Maya: We'll draft a decision tree: managed-hosted (fastest), dedicated (isolated GPUs, reserved capacity), and private (customer-managed control plane). Each has tradeoffs on latency and cost. We'll attach that to the ref arch doc.
[08:55] 
[09:10] Diego: One technical caveat — for low-latency inference we rely on local NVMe-backed KV caches and shared memory between inference pods; that requires ephemeral local storage and appropriate taints/tolerations on the nodes. For Helio's managed K8s, we need nodegroup profile with local NVMe.
[09:35] Liam: We do have a node pool with local NVMe. We'll add the node label example in the infra docs.
[09:45] Diego: Great. Also quantization builds and kernel selection — sometimes references in transcripts show 'kernel selection' as 'kernel election' — we'll be sending the runtime notes.
[10:05] Priya: For private deployments we also need a rollback plan in case a new model causes regressions. How do you do rollouts?
[10:20] Anika: We support canary rollouts, A/B routing and automatic fallback to a baseline model. The ref arch will include a rollout policy example and SLOs to monitor.
[10:35] Rajiv: Does Redwood have SOC2 artifacts to share? Our procurement needs that for the listing.
[10:45] Maya: Yes — we'll attach the SOC 2 Type II cert and our security whitepaper to the share. We'll also provide a short compliance manifest with key controls.
[11:05] Priya: On customer data residency, can we pin storage to Helio's region?
[11:15] Diego: Yes, we can configure region-scoped storage buckets and regional inference endpoints. We'll document region config in the manifest.
[11:30] 
[11:45] Liam: A practical question: do you support Helm values overrides for marketplace installs so we can set custom ingress and oidc configs?
[11:58] Anika: Yes, the chart supports values.yaml overrides and have examples for ingress controllers (nginx, contour) and oidc connector entries. We'll include sample values for Helio's environment.
[12:20] Priya: Networking again, we need to decide VPC peering vs PrivateLink. Any recommendation?
[12:35] Diego: PrivateLink (private endpoints) reduces cross-account route table complexity but has some limits on IP addresses. VPC peering is straightforward but you must manage route tables and security groups. We'll document both with tradeoffs in the ref arch.
[12:55] Priya: Ok. For the test harness, can Redwood run the acceptance suite inside our CI (Helio's pipeline) or do you want to run it from Redwood's CI?
[13:10] Diego: We can do either. Preferred is to run our suite in a cross-account job that Helio triggers, so results are reproducible and logs can be forwarded to your observability. We'll provide the github actions / tekton templates.
[13:30] Liam: We'll need the RBAC service account for that job.
[13:38] Diego: We'll request a service account with minimal perms in the test org.
[13:45] 
[14:00] Anika: Quick note on manifest notarization: Helio requires a checksum and signature. Our CI will produce a signed artifact using our signing key; Helio can verify the signature and checksum during listing.
[14:20] Rajiv: We need to review the signing key policy. Can Redwood rotate keys and provide key metadata?
[14:32] Diego: Yes, we support key rotation and will include metadata and rotation windows.
[14:40] 
[14:50] Maya: Let's capture the main blockers: 1) exchange test account/service principal, 2) finalize manifest schema mapping for metering, 3) finalize network pattern recommendation, 4) security docs for SOC2/KMS. Anything else?
[15:05] Priya: Also need a sample SLA and support path for marketplace customers.
[15:15] Maya: We'll include a draft SLA with the listing materials.
[15:22] 
[15:40] Diego: One more technical note — when deploying in private mode, the control plane agent needs egress to our update endpoints for kernel patches; some customers block egress entirely. We can provide an air-gapped package but it's heavier. We'll document the air-gap install steps too.
[16:05] Liam: We have a few sensitive customers who will want air-gapped installs. Good to have that captured.
[16:20] Priya: On metrics, what telemetry do you emit for SLOs? We'll want to map to our dashboards.
[16:30] Anika: We emit per-route latency, per-model token counts, cache hit rates, and node-level GPU utilization. We'll provide prometheus scrape configs and Grafana dashboard JSON.
[16:55] Rajiv: That will be helpful for our security and ops reviews.
[17:05] 
[17:20] Maya: Ok, next steps recap — Diego and Anika will share the manifest/helm draft + playbook, Maya will share marketing blurb, Helio to spin up test org and share credentials. We also agreed to meet next week for a demo of the CI test-run.
[17:45] Priya: Sounds good. One question — are there any known limitations on quantized models and on-prem GPUs we should be aware of?
[17:58] Diego: Some older GPUs have driver quirks with int8 kernels; we'll list recommended driver and cuda versions.
[18:15] Liam: We'll check our GPU node groups and align.
[18:25] 
[18:40] Maya: Any final questions?
[18:45] Sofia: No, we'll wait for the manifest and the copy.
[18:50] Priya: Please include a short checklist for procurement so our legal team can speed up the listing.
[19:02] Maya: Will do.
[19:10] Diego: I'll follow up with the CI templates and a sample runbook link.
[19:20] 
[20:00] -- end of main Q&A, rest of call used to walk through a quick demo of the Helm install (screen share) and a short walkthrough of the ref arch doc.

[30:00] Diego (during demo): "kubectl apply -f redwood-helm.yaml", then we set values: storageClass=nvme-local, nodeSelector=redwood-nvme, tolerations, and set the meter-proxy secret. Demo had some slurred words on the text overlay, transcription shows typos.

[38:12] Liam: We ran into an issue with the ingress controller in our staging cluster earlier — will the chart support contour out of the box?
[38:30] Anika: Yes, contour, nginx, and alb supported. We'll add a sample values for contour with SNI.

[45:00] Rajiv: Security team will review the manifest and run a pen test once the QA harness is in place. Expect us to send a prioritized list.

[51:20] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll circulate notes and action items. Talk soon.

End of transcript.
